crop.notes: Full article with headline and subheads.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic reported that veteran pugilist Tom Allen was confined to his bed at his Market Street home with severe colds, and recalled his fights with Davis, Goss and Mace.

facts.fact: Allen lay seriously ill with persistent colds at his home on Market Street between Sixth and Seventh
Allen was born in 1839 and began his ring career at about 21
Allen knocked out Charlie Davis in five rounds in England, the first championship fight under Queensberry rules, winning a purse of 190 pounds and a silver cup that hangs over his bar
Allen fought Joe Goss for the heavyweight championship; the bout ended in a riot and Allen's seconds were mobbed
Allen fought Jem Mace in Louisiana for the heavyweight championship and $5,000; his seconds threw up the sponge after ten rounds (50 minutes) when Allen hurt his arm
Allen beat Mike McCool in seven rounds on Bloody Island

notes: Article says he fought Goss in 1867 (other records say 1876); and that he knocked out Davis, which is Allen's English win. Don Murphy is named as his manager.
